issues.failure_explanation: The $Z$-component of $F_{t_{n,i}}(t_{n,j},\cdot)$ carries the factor $\Delta W_{t_{n,i},t_{n,j}}^{\top}/(t_{n,j}-t_{n,i})$, which is not a.s. bounded, so the a.s. $\mathcal{O}$-calculus used in the proof does not apply to it. The Taylor remainder of order $r$ in $R^{n,j}$ in (eq_EtniDelFninj) is, for that component, $\frac{1}{r!}\mathbb{E}_{t_{n,i}}[\partial_\theta^r f(\xi)(R^{n,j})^{\otimes r}\Delta W^{\top}]/((c_i-c_j)\Delta t_n)$; with only the a.s. bound $R^{n,j}=\mathcal{O}(\Delta t)$ from (eq_preest_Rni) this is $\mathcal{O}((\Delta t)^{r}\cdot(\Delta t)^{-1/2})$, and after multiplication by $\Delta t_n$ in (eq_expand_dtDF) only $\mathcal{O}((\Delta t)^{r+1/2})$, not the claimed $\mathcal{O}((\Delta t)^{r+1})$. Similarly, the justification of (eq_preest_Rni) ignores the second term of (eq_RniEni), which again contains the Brownian factor. No argument (e.g. Stein-type integration by parts requiring $x$-derivative bounds of $R^{n,j}$, or an extra Taylor order plus $\mathbb{E}_t|\Delta W_{t,s}|\lesssim\sqrt{s-t}$) is given to close the half-order loss.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the Taylor expansion in (eq_EtniDelFninj) to order $l\le r$ (the extra trees have order $\ge r+1$ and fall into the remainder), bound remainder terms containing $\Delta W_{t,s}/(s-t)$ via $\mathbb{E}_t|\Delta W_{t,s}|\le C\sqrt{s-t}$ so the loss is compensated, and state/prove (via Stein's identity under Assumption assu_regu) that the elementary differentials $F^{\Upsilon}_{t,s}$ are a.s. bounded uniformly for $s$ near $t$; also justify (eq_preest_Rni) by the same induction.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the induction in the proof of Theorem thm_taylor does not establish the remainder order $(\Delta t)^{r+1}$ for the $Z$-part of the expansion; hence the consistency statement (eq_maxRn) and the convergence results built on it are not fully supported.
issues.title: Remainder orders in the error expansion ignore the unbounded factor $\Delta W_{t,s}/(s-t)$ in $F_t$
issues.why_classification: A genuine gap in the key inductive remainder estimate, but a contained additional argument (one more Taylor order plus conditional moment bounds for the Brownian factor) closes it without changing the theorem's conclusion or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: In (eq0_Etni_med)/(eq_defHikl) the sum runs over ordered tuples $(\Upsilon_1,\dots,\Upsilon_l)$, and by Definition def_tree0 (branches are ordered, cf. fig_ntree where the class of $[[[\;]_4[\;]_4]_2[\;]_3]_1$ has exactly two elements) the map $(k,\Upsilon_1,\dots,\Upsilon_l)\mapsto[\Upsilon_1\cdots\Upsilon_l]_k$ is a bijection onto $\widetilde{\T}(r)$. Hence $\tilde I_i=\sum_{\Upsilon\in\widetilde{\T}(r)}B_i^m(\Upsilon)(\Delta t_n)^{|\Upsilon|}F^{\Upsilon}$ with no factor $N_P(\Upsilon)$; the second equality of (eq_tildeIi) is invalid. Concretely, for $\Upsilon=[[\;]_0[\;]_0]_0$ a direct computation gives the term $\frac12\Delta t_n\sum_j a_{ij}A_j^m([\;]_0)^2(\Delta t_n)^2 F_{\theta\theta}(F,F)$, whereas (eq2_Rnj_indc) with $\alpha=1$, $S=2$, $\gamma=2$ asserts coefficient $1\cdot A_0^m(\Upsilon)$, off by the factor $S=2$. The correct coefficients are $\alpha(\Upsilon)/\gamma(\Upsilon)$ (LN-tree level $1/\gamma$); the stated ones $\alpha S/\gamma$ are wrong for every tree with repeated identical branches.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $S(\Upsilon)/\gamma(\Upsilon)$ by $1/\gamma(\Upsilon)$ in (eq_Rnj_indc), (eq_expandEni), (eq_deftildeAi), and $\alpha S/\gamma$ by $\alpha/\gamma$ in (eq2_Rnj_indc); drop the $N_P$ insertion in (eq_defBim)/(eq_tildeIi) so that $B_i^m(\Upsilon)=A_i^m(\Upsilon)/\gamma(\Upsilon)$ follows directly from the bijection.
issues.overall_effect: The error expansion (eq2_Rnj_indc), advertised as one of the main results, has incorrect coefficients (extra factor $S(\Upsilon)\ge1$); the tabulated $S$ values in the supplement are irrelevant to the true expansion. Since $S\ne0$, the order conditions (eq_ord_cond1), $C(r)$ and Theorem thm_consistent, which use only vanishing of $A_0^m$, remain valid.
issues.title: Spurious factor $N_P(\Upsilon)$ when re-indexing ordered branch tuples as LN-trees; expansion coefficient $\alpha S/\gamma$ is wrong
issues.why_classification: The theorem as stated is false (wrong explicit coefficients) and a proof step is invalid, but a systematic, non-lossy correction yields a comparable expansion and all order-condition consequences survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Passing from (eq_estEtniDelFtnij) to (eq_estDelFtnij) replaces $\mathbb{E}[\rho^2(\mathbb{E}_{t_{n,j}}X-\mathbb{E}_{t_{n,i}}X)]$ by $\mathbb{E}[\rho^2(X)]-\mathbb{E}[\rho^2(\mathbb{E}_{t_n}X)]$, which is the orthogonality of martingale increments and holds only for seminorms induced by a semi-inner product. For a general seminorm it fails: with $\rho(y)=|y_1|+|y_2|$ on $\R^2$, trivial $\mathcal{F}_t$ and $X\in\{(1,0),(0,1)\}$ equiprobable, the left side is $1$ while the right side is $1-1=0$. Assumption assu_FLipVar only requires $\rho$ to be a seminorm.

issues.failure_explanation: Inserting (eq_estEpho2Ephi) into (eq_rkEn2) produces the negative term $-C C_{\pi_N}^2\frac{(\Delta t)^2}{\Delta t_n}\mathbb{E}[\rho^2(\mathbb{E}_{t_n}\mathcal{E}^{n+1})]$. Since $\Delta t_n\le\Delta t$ one only has $(\Delta t)^2/\Delta t_n\ge\Delta t$, so the term is at most $-CC_{\pi_N}^2\Delta t\,\mathbb{E}[\rho^2(\mathbb{E}_{t_n}\mathcal{E}^{n+1})]$; the proof writes $-CC_{\pi_N}^3\Delta t(\dots)$, which requires $(\Delta t)^2/\Delta t_n\ge C_{\pi_N}\Delta t$, false unless $\Delta t_n$ is the minimal step. The subsequent exact cancellation of the $\mathbb{E}[\rho^2(\mathbb{E}_{t_n}\mathcal{E}^{n+1})]$ terms via $\delta_2=(CC_{\pi_N}^3)^{-1}$ therefore rests on an invalid inequality (the following line also mixes $C_{\pi_N}^2$ and $C_{\pi_N}^3$).
